question: A 35-year-old male patient is brought into the emergency department by emergency medical services. The patient has a history of schizophrenia and is on medication per his mother. His mother also states that the dose of his medication was recently increased, though she is not sure of the specific medication he takes. His vitals are HR 110, BP 170/100, T 102.5, RR 22. On exam, he cannot respond to questions and has rigidity. His head is turned to the right and remains in that position during the exam. Labs are significant for a WBC count of 14,000 cells/mcL, with a creatine kinase (CK) level of 3,000 mcg/L. What is the best treatment for this patient?
analysis: The patient is presenting with symptoms consistent with neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS), which is a rare but potentially life-threatening side effect of antipsychotic medications. The elevated CK levels and rigidity are concerning for this diagnosis. The best treatment for NMS is immediate discontinuation of the offending medication and supportive care. Dantrolene is a muscle relaxant that can be used to manage the muscle rigidity and hyperthermia associated with NMS.
